newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: FORECAST - Pakistan vegoil consumption seen rising.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Pakistan vegoil consumption seen rising.

text.p: Pakistan's oils and fats consumption is likely to rise steadily over the next five years, with domestic oilseed production unable to match growing demand, a Malaysian palm oil expert said on Tuesday.

Mamat Bin Salleh of Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority told a seminar in Karachi that consumption could reach 2.65 million tonnes by the year 2000 from 2.39 million in 1995, against 2.07 million tonnes in 1991.
Demand was stoked by population growth, urbanisation, higher per capita income, competitive prices and the participation of the private sector in the import trade, Salleh said.
He said Pakistan's domestic production of oils and fats had averaged 0.84 million tonnes a year from 1991 to 1995.

"In 1995, Pakistan produced about 374,000 tonnes of cottonseed oil, 66,000 tonnes of rapeseed oil and 30,000 tonnes of sunflower oil, 10,000 tonnes of coconut/soya oil and 380,000 tonnes of butter," Salleh said.
"Pakistan is importing about 60 percent of its oils and fats requirements, ranging from 1.0 million tonnes to 1.5 million tonnes per annum over the past five years," he said.
Salleh said it was difficult to assess future domestic oilseeds production, but said it could reach one million tonnes by the year 2000.
"It can be expected that within the next five years, the domestic production will be able to meet only a portion of the total demand," he added.
Malaysia remains Pakistan's top supplier, but Indonesia has emerged as a new source, selling about 50,000 tonnes of palm oil a year. Salleh said this trade pattern was likely to continue.
The role of Singapore middlemen had declined, with traders and importers preferring to buy direct from producers, he added.
Pakistan imported 1.143 million tonnes of edible oil worth $855 million in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June), compared to 1.395 million tonnes worth $997 million in 1994/95, official figures show.
